claim: Code-side scoring of candidate questions by expected information gain over a sampled hypothesis set beats asking the LLM to pick an informative question, in guessing and diagnosis games. BED-LLM mean over 18 cells (6 LLMs x 3 sets, Table 1, cross-checker mean): Prompt-Only 30.3, CoT 39.5, Split 55.4, Entropy 57.6, full EIG 70.7 percent. UoT gains over direct prompting on 20 Questions, diagnosis and troubleshooting; ATD gains on code tasks.
agent_test: Same model, same token budget: LLM picks the probe vs sample N candidate probes and score them in code, on 100 diagnosis items; report success and tokens.

claim: The cheap half-split rule (pick the question that splits sampled hypotheses most evenly) recovers most of the gain: by our mean over Table 1 cells, Split gains 25.1 of 40.4 points (about 62 percent) of the full-EIG gain over Prompt-Only. Full EIG adds about 15 points more. Only one paper measures this.
schema_part: S7 probe choice; half-split as default
agent_test: Compare half-split, entropy and full EIG at equal tokens on the probe step.

claim: Explicit chain-of-thought about which question is best does not close the gap to computed EIG (CoT 39.5 vs EIG 70.7 mean; Llama-3.3-70B Animals CoT 40 = Prompt-Only 40). CoT is not strictly below Split in every cell (Things GPT-4o 49 vs 40).
agent_test: Ablate: prompt-only, CoT, computed score; same token budget.

claim: Belief handling is critical: sampled hypotheses must be filtered against the interaction history. Raw in-context beliefs collapse (Animals GPT-4o-mini 18 vs 88 percent).
agent_test: Keep an explicit hypothesis list and filter it by every observation; compare to implicit memory.

claim: The source of probabilities matters: the model's own log-probs over candidates are a worse weighting than uniform weight over sampled candidates (rank score 3.9 vs 6.3, Llama3-70B, 10 questions).
agent_test: Score probes with uniform sample weights vs the model's own stated probabilities.

claim: Gains shrink as the base model gets stronger or the task gets softer: HumanEval gap of EIG over base at 4 questions is about 15 points for GPT-3.5 (binary) but about 2 for GPT-4o-mini; preference elicitation and MediQ-style transfer gains are small or within noise.
schema_part: S7 gating: probe only when uncertainty is high
agent_test: Measure gain vs base accuracy; trigger the probing procedure only above an uncertainty threshold.

claim: Information-gain probing works best when answers cleanly eliminate hypotheses and a finite candidate set exists. Soft answers and open candidate sets weaken it.
agent_test: Test on items with soft answers; compare with and without an enumerated candidate list.

claim: Reward choice inside the lookahead matters little: information gain, uncertainty-reduction and split rewards are within 1-3 points of each other (GPT-3.5, UoT Table 3); the tree lookahead may do more of the work. PFS is clearly worse only on 20Q-BIG-bench (37.9 vs 51.7).
schema_part: O probe scoring; keep it simple
agent_test: Compare simple split score vs full EIG vs tree lookahead at equal tokens.

claim: Putting the Bayes update, EIG and stopping in code and using the LLM only to parse answers beat frontier LLMs doing everything: MoBayes top-1 78 vs 60 percent on DDxPlus (n=50 per cell, wide CIs).
agent_test: Give the agent a code tool that holds the posterior over hypotheses; compare to LLM-only tracking.

claim: Un-scaffolded LLMs are poor at multi-turn probe choice: GPT-4 wins 0.31 (Things) and 0.50 (Celebrities) of 20Q games; failure modes are early enumeration and repeated questions. Humans scored 0.24 and 0.31 in the same table.
agent_test: Log repeated or already-answered probes and early specific guesses in the agent traces.

claim: Scaffolded orchestration with explicit hypothesis tracking and cost awareness improved sequential diagnosis: o3 baseline 78.6% at $7,850 vs MAI-DxO no-budget 81.9% at $4,735 vs budgeted 79.9% at $2,396 vs ensemble 85.5% at $7,184. No paper ablates the roles: MAI-DxO varies budget and ensembling only, and on o3 and o4-mini the accuracy gain was not significant (the cost cut was). A non-medical troubleshooting study with a component ablation (SIA) shows the challenger-style role worth about 5 points and follow-up questions about 4 points.
agent_test: Add a cost steward step and explicit differential; ablate each at equal tokens.

claim: Cost-weighted probing: with one fault and independent components, the optimal order is by probability over observation cost; with equal cost and probability this reduces to halving. The general optimal policy is intractable (NP-complete).
agent_test: Order candidate checks by p/cost in a code tool; compare with unordered checking. Primary papers for Hyafil-Rivest, Kadane-Simon, Heckerman not opened.

claim: Greedy (myopic) probe choice is a sound default: under adaptive submodularity it is log-factor competitive with the best policy for noise-free answers. The proven factor is (ln Q + 1)^2 for self-certifying instances; the earlier single-log claim was withdrawn and is open. Read 'near optimal' as worst-case logarithmic, not as a percentage.
agent_test: None needed; use as justification.

claim: Greedy one-step EIG ignores later steps; learned or non-myopic policies can do better, mainly when a test is useless alone but useful later. LLM evidence is small and partly in an appendix. In UoT, one-step lookahead reached about 89% (medical), 98% (troubleshooting) and 84% (20 Questions) of the depth-3 success rate.
agent_test: Test K=2 lookahead vs K=1 at equal tokens on tasks with enabling tests.

claim: Entropy-based selection can fail under model misspecification (the same wrong model chooses and interprets data); in GDE, entropy over a huge diagnosis set is intractable and pruning to a few probable diagnoses lowers compute but may raise measurement counts. With an open, LLM-proposed hypothesis space, max-information queries can also collapse the proposal pool (Number Game: EIG did not beat random on easy rules).
agent_test: Add a rule: periodically choose a probe that could falsify the leading hypothesis; compare.

claim: In GDE-style circuit diagnosis, combining failure probability with wire entropy cut measurements sharply vs random order and entropy alone (c432 single fault: 92.3 random, 42.0 entropy, 6.7 combined). Not re-verified this pass.
agent_test: Test on fault-finding tasks where priors come from past failure rates.

claim: Inference-time EIG with LLM-built models is expensive and not always better on reasoning models: BED-LLM took 2376 s per game (61.1 times a trained policy) and gave only modest gains over a reasoning base, sometimes worse. Authors reimplemented BED-LLM themselves. New: thinking helps selection only partly (Qwen3 thinking picks the max-information candidate in 19-36% of turns); QuestBench: o1-preview and Gemini thinking stay near 40-50% on logic and planning while BFS depth 10 gets 99.8%.
agent_test: Report tokens and wall time next to accuracy; compare to a reasoning-model baseline at equal tokens.

claim: Proposer quality matters less than the selection rule: a hand-made random proposer reranked by information gain matches an LLM proposer (6.55 vs 6.55 at 10 candidates in Zendo), and more candidates help (5.84, 6.23, 6.55).
agent_test: Vary the number of candidate probes (1, 5, 10) with a fixed selection rule.

claim: Naive question-asking can make clinical diagnosis worse than receiving the same limited case (MediQ: average 11.3% relative drop; most samples get zero questions). A separate 'should I ask' gate recovers it: MediQ confidence 1-5 with rationale and 3-sample consistency beat ask-always by 22.3% and closed 51.2% of the gap to full information, but the threshold was grid-searched. In coding, a separate binary underspecification checker raised resolve rate from 61.2% to 69.4% (Claude Sonnet 4.5, 500 tasks) and asked only when needed.
agent_test: Compare ask-always, ask-when-uncertain, no-ask.

claim: Fine-tuning for informative questions (DPO on EIG pairs, behavior cloning, RL) raises success in-domain but is training, outside our constraint; transfer is uneven (MediQ transfer +0.9 points for ASIG; +4.2 points in Kriz dermatology).
agent_test: Skip; use only as an upper bound.

claim: Uncertainty of Thoughts '38.1%' is a mean relative improvement over direct prompting, not points. Re-derived from Table 1: Llama3-70B 46.6% relative (matches paper) but +10.1 points; the other models +9.2 to +12.8 points. No independent replication of UoT was found in this search.
agent_test: When citing UoT in the schema notes, say about +10 points absolute.

claim: At matched GPT-4 token cost, uncertainty-scored question selection beats tree search with self-scored reward and self-consistency (about 4.6k tokens: pruned UoT 48.1/88.4/63.2 vs Adapted-ToT 33.8/85.1/60.3 vs CoT-SC 32.6/37.6/42.5 on 20Q/medical/troubleshooting). Nobody has tested it against a reasoning model given the same tokens.
agent_test: Equal-token arms on 100 items: (a) reasoning model with N thinking tokens, (b) same model with sampled candidate probes scored in code, (c) half-split on sampled hypotheses.

claim: Reasoning models still leave probe-selection headroom: they gain information per turn when hypotheses are hidden, yet pick the best of their own candidates in 19-36% of turns (Qwen3, Guess My City); QuestBench shows thinking models near 40-50% on logic and planning while a depth-10 search gets 99.8%; for o3 on MAI-DxO the scaffold's effect was mainly cost, not accuracy. Reasoning fine-tuning also lowers abstention (AbstentionBench abstract, 24% average).
schema_part: O probe generation vs selection; S7 gate
agent_test: Run the same probe-selection task with a thinking model and a non-thinking model plus code-side scoring.

claim: Models recognise that a question is ambiguous much more often than they act on it: clarifying questions are about 5% at best on ambiguous queries (Su and Cardie), most MediQ samples had zero questions, and retrieved context makes asking rarer. A separate forced gate is what changes behaviour.
agent_test: Compare self-initiated probing vs a gate step that forces a probe when the leading hypothesis share is below a set value.

claim: A value-of-information rule (ask only if expected utility gain exceeds the cost of asking) matched or beat the best tuned confidence threshold in most cost settings with no tuning, but lost at high question cost (Gemini Mixed 20Q: +0.34 to +1.36 at costs 0.01-0.05; -0.90 and -0.96 at 0.10 and 0.20). Costs are user-effort numbers, not probe prices.
agent_test: Price a probe in tokens or wall-clock and test VoI-gated probing against fixed-threshold probing.

claim: When hypotheses are proposed by an LLM from an open space, maximum-information probes can backfire: they eliminate most particles, the proposer then yields invalid or over-specific hypotheses, and convergence stalls (odd numbers: EIG 7 queries vs positive-test 4 vs random 2). On compound rules the order reverses (even numbers below 30: EIG 17 vs positive-test 31; digits sum below 8: EIG 43 vs positive-test DNF), so positive-test probes are faster on easy rules and fail to falsify on compound ones. A switch rule (safe probes first, falsifying probes when stalled) is proposed but untested.
agent_test: Compare max-entropy, leader-falsifying and positive-test probes on fixation-prone debugging items; log the fixation rate.

claim: No study isolates which MAI-DxO role saves money. Best split available: panel alone cut cost 39.7% with +3.3 points (o3); budget tracker cut a further 2,339 dollars at -2.0 points; ensembling added +3.6 points at the baseline cost. Outside medicine, SIA's ablation shows removing the counterfactual role costs 5.2 points and removing follow-up questions 4.2 points.
agent_test: Ablate challenger, steward and ensemble separately on the same probe task.

claim: Cheap rules on probe form can move results as much as computed scoring: in open-ended GuessingGame, forbidding repeated question types or forcing open questions took LLaMA-3.3 70B from 39.4% to 80.0% and 97.4%, GPT-4o from 64.1% to 98.5%, with no extra compute. Compare these before paying for sampling and scoring.
agent_test: Add a no-repeat-type rule to the baseline arm in the equal-token test.

claim: Answer noise is the least tested piece. Gains survive a mismatched answerer model (BED-LLM) and an open hypothesis list (UoT open set: +9.8 points vs +10.9 closed), and shrink on a soft free-text task (film preference). Nobody injected wrong or inconsistent answers into EIG-driven probing; Text-to-SQL authors list it as future work.
agent_test: Flip 10-20% of probe answers and measure the drop for scored and unscored probing.

claim: Failure-rate priors for an LLM agent are untested. Probability-over-cost ordering is proven optimal only under single fault, independent costs and few observation types (Breese and Heckerman), with priors taken from a device model. The only LLM prior ablation is a low-trust synthetic study (176 vs 387 errors, empirical vs uniform prior).
agent_test: On debugging items, rank suspects by prior (from repository history) over probe cost vs uniform; measure probes to find the fault.

claim: Original GDE and de Kleer 1992/2006 lookahead numbers were not obtained. What was read: de Kleer 1991 says minimum-entropy GDE uses one step because there are very many diagnoses, and does full lookahead when about five leading diagnoses are kept; UoT shows one step gets 84-98% of depth 3; Golovin and Krause give a worst-case log-squared bound.
agent_test: Use one-step scoring by default; test two-step only where a probe is costly or irreversible.
